newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea intervenes again to support won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea intervenes again to support won.

text.p: South Korea's central bank stepped in again in mid-afternoon trading to stop the won from falling against the U.S. dollar following a similar move earlier on Friday, dealers said.
In the latest move, the Bank of Korea sold dollars at 842.80 won, they said.
The central bank had sold dollars in early morning trading when the won slipped to 845.00.
"The central bank's will to stop the won from falling further appears to be strong," said a local bank dealer.
They said dollar demand was rising because of expected import settlements.
The won rose to 841.90 minutes after the afternoon intervention, but later fell back to 842.50 at 0530 GMT.
